_meta.sourceDocument: Legend in the Mist — Core Rulebook (Son of Oak Game Studio), plus the named supplements (Action Grimoire, The Oracle, Character Pack).
_meta.sourceEdition: UNVERIFIED. The Core Rulebook PDF/text is NOT present in this repository or build environment. Rules content in the app was originally extracted via the project's NotebookLM notebook 'Legend In The Mist: Core Rulebook' (id ee1b1502-78a0-4b9e-9e26-a0662816ec0b).
_meta.provenance: SEEDED from CLAUDE.md (this project's own documentation + roadmap). Entries were NOT cross-checked against the Core Rulebook text, because that text is unavailable here. Per the coverage-audit protocol's 'Seeding' clause, this buys regression detection now while omission detection stays inactive.
caveats: This file proves a MAPPING (documented feature -> code artefact). It does NOT prove correctness: a marker can exist while the code holds wrong values or wrong behaviour. Where correctness is asserted, it is by the reachability/behaviour scripts, not this one.

OMISSION detection is NOT active: a genuine Core Rulebook requirement that was never written into CLAUDE.md is simply absent from this list and would go undetected. Fixing this requires the actual rulebook, worked section by section.

'implemented' here means: a code marker for the feature was confirmed present in character-tracker.html (so regression detection is live for it). It does NOT mean the behaviour was verified against the rulebook.
Supplement features (Action Grimoire, The Oracle, Character Pack) are cited to their supplement, not the Core Book.

statusMeaning.implemented: code marker confirmed present in the built app (regression-detected).
statusMeaning.partial: implemented but with a stated gap — see note.
statusMeaning.deliberately-omitted: documented out-of-scope — see note; marker is null.
statusMeaning.unknown: requirement/implementation not yet verified against the source — see note.

_meta.howToExtend: Obtain the Core Rulebook, read a section, and add one entry per discrete requirement: stable id, source citation (page/section), one-line summary in the book's own terms, and the MOST SPECIFIC code marker that would disappear if the feature were removed (a function/const/element-id substring present in character-tracker.html). New requirements start 'unknown' until their marker is found. Run: node scripts/coverage.js

entries.summary: An action is resolved by rolling 2d6 and adding Power.
Power = +1 per helpful tag, -1 per hindering tag, plus highest helpful status tier minus highest hindering.
10+ full success; 7-9 success with a consequence; 6- consequence.
Double sixes = automatic success; double ones = automatic consequence, regardless of Power.
On a success you always have at least 1 Power to spend.
Burn a tag for +3 instead of +1; the tag is scratched.
Task Might vs your Might yields Favored (+3/+6) or Imperiled (-3/-6).
Reaction: 10+ spend Power+1 on any effect; 7-9 spend only to lessen; 6- take as-is.

entries.source: Core Book — Spending Power on Effects
entries.summary: Spend Power to create/recover tags, inflict/reduce statuses, discover a detail, or take an extra feat.
Other Heroes can contribute helping/hindering tags to an action.
Statuses have tiers 1-6; applying one marks its tier's box, spilling right if taken.
A Hero's Limit is 5 (overcome at 5, killed/transformed at 6); a Challenge/foe may have Limit 1-6.
Reducing a status shifts its marks down by the tiers removed.
Statuses belong to a Hero or a foe; foe statuses are tracked per target.
Progress tracks advance toward a Limit (projects, chases, unlocks, breakthroughs).
A Hero is defined by (typically four) theme cards.
20 theme types grouped by Might (Origin/Adventure/Greatness/Any).
Themes carry power tags (help) and weakness tags (hinder; invoking a weakness marks Improve).
The Backpack holds story tags, flipped helpful/hindering, scratched when single-use.
Scratched tags are used up until recovered (e.g., by resting at camp).
A Promise track of 5 records advancement.
Reaching 5 Promise triggers a Moment of Fulfillment: reset Promise (carry overflow), gain a reward.
Permanent, rule-breaking qualities gained at a Moment of Fulfillment.
Quintessences with mechanical effects change how rolls/play resolve.
entries.note: Only Beyond Luck is auto-encoded in the roller (removes the double-ones auto-miss). Other mechanical Quintessences (Larger Than Life, Lucky Bastard, Virtuoso, Loyal Companion, etc.) are stored as recorded text and applied manually by the player; there is no per-Quintessence auto-trigger UI.

entries.summary: Each theme has Improve/Milestone/Abandon tracks; filling one (3) develops the theme.
Each theme type offers Special Improvements, chosen as the theme improves (5 per type).
Extra parts of an abandoned/replaced theme can be traded for +1 Promise each.
A shared fifth theme any Hero can invoke; its power tags are single-use.
A single-use relationship tag per fellow Hero.
Environment/temporary story tags exist in the current scene.

entries.source: Core Book — Playing the Game (the loop)
entries.summary: The play loop: Establish the scene, take Action, resolve Consequences.
Expire tags, establish the place, take activities (Rest/Reflect/Camp Action), recover a Fellowship part.
A journey montage with legs to arrival, a time-passes clock, and vignette challenges.
28 Tropes (three themes plus a suggested fourth) as a quick-start path.
20 themebooks with power/weakness tag questions and quest ideas (the Detailed path).

entries.source: Core Book — Hero Creation / Theme Kits
entries.summary: Per-type theme kits: choose 2 power + 1 weakness tag and a suggested Quest.
entries.note: One known PDF-parser artefact remains: Relic -> 'Heirloom Longsword' has a merged weakness/quest tag (cosmetic, editable on the sheet). Otherwise the 113 kits parse cleanly.

entries.source: Core Book — Hero Creation / General Store
entries.summary: Suggested starting Backpack items to pick from.
entries.note: Implemented as an EXPANDED CURATED suggestions aid (17 categories / ~217 items in _build/general-store.json), not a verbatim reproduction of the Core Book's General Store table. Players can type their own. Fidelity of the exact book list is unverified.

entries.summary: 6 Fellowship kits plus a per-fellow relationship table.

Verbatim worked cost+effect spend examples grouped by scenario.
Full standalone action catalog: 19 leaf action sections (101 entries) + 2 prose sections.
The Gerrin introductory walkthrough.
20 ready-made Heroes importable at full fidelity.
Solo/co-op oracle tools, gated behind a Solo Play mode.
Interpretive (d66 symbol) and Yes/No (2d6 +/- Power, extreme on doubles) question oracles.
Roll a whole scene across seven columns; re-roll any single column.
Roll an area then a creature/person/place, plus a vignette.
Build a Challenge Profile: Mighty aspects, CR, Limits, tags/statuses, consequences.
Pick one of 11 Roles, roll d6 for its Threat/Consequence.
Roll d66 for a consequence category plus a specific d6 consequence.
Pick Act I/II/III and roll d66 for a revelation.
A per-hero oracle log/journal with a note per entry.
The full menu of consequence types/severities the Narrator can inflict.
entries.note: Not verified against the Core Rulebook's consequence rules. The app surfaces the Oracle supplement's solo Consequences tables as a player-side approximation; whether that covers the Core Book's consequence framework is unchecked (requires the rulebook).
